text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on March 4 in history.
1193 - Saladin, Sultan of Egypt and Syria, died. His forces captured Jerusalem in 1187, ending its 88-year occupation by the Franks.
1394 - Portuguese explorer Prince Henry the Navigator born. He sponsored expeditions along the African coast which led to the foundation of the overseas Portuguese empire.
1461 - King Henry VI of England was deposed and succeeded by Edward IV.
1678 - Antonio Vivaldi, Italian composer, best known for "The Four Seasons", born.
1681 - King Charles II granted William Penn almost all of what is now Pennsylvania.
1789 - The first U.S. Congress convened in New York City.
1791 - Vermont became the 14th state of the United States.
1793 - George Washington was inaugurated for a second term as president of the United States.
1801 - Thomas Jefferson became the first U.S. president to be inaugurated in the new capital of Washington.
1824 - The Royal National Lifeboat Institution was founded.
1832 - Jean-Francois Champollion, French historian and Egyptologist, died.
1877 - Tchaikovsky's ballet "Swan Lake" was first performed at the Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow.
1913 - Woodrow Wilson was inaugurated as the 28th U.S. president.
1927 - Some 25,000 diggers participated in a rush to stake their claims in new diamond fields at Grasfontein, South Africa.
1933 - Franklin D. Roosevelt was sworn in as 32nd U.S. president.
1941 - A British naval raid on the German-occupied Lofoten Islands off Norway sank 11 German ships.
1964 - U.N. Security Council adopted a resolution to appoint a mediator and establish a U.N. peace-keeping force in Cyprus.
1970 - The French submarine Eurydice sank off the coast of Toulon. All 57 aboard died.
1971 - Canadian Prime Minister Pierre Trudeau secretly married Margaret Sinclair.
1974 - British Prime Minister Edward Heath resigned; Labour leader Harold Wilson formed a new government.
1975 - Actor Charlie Chaplin was knighted at Buckingham Palace.
1976 - In Northern Ireland, the Ulster Convention was formally dissolved.
1977 - Over 1,570 people were killed in Romania by an earthquake which registered 7.2 on the Richter scale; 35,000 families were made homeless.
1980 - Rhodesian governor Lord Soames invited Robert Mugabe to form a government after his ZANU-PF party won a decisive election victory.
1990 - President Lennox Sebe was ousted in a military coup in the South African homeland of Ciskei.
1991 - Coup leader Idriss Deby was sworn in as Chad's new president.
1991 - The Soviet parliament ratified a six-nation treaty setting the legal seal on German unification after two years of revolutionary change in central Europe.
1991 - Miners in the two largest Soviet coalfields went on strike to support demands for the resignation of President Mikhail Gorbachev and for pay rises.
1991 - Crown Prince Sheikh Saad al-Abdulla al-Sabah became the first senior member of the Kuwaiti ruling family to return to the homeland liberated from Iraqi occupation.
1994 - Four Moslem fundamentalists were found guilty of bombing the landmark World Trade Centre in New York.
1994 - Zulu chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi and white separatist Constand Viljoen signed up at the last moment to contest South Africa's multi-racial elections.
1996 - A Moslem suicide bomber killed 13 people and wounded 100, including children, outside a crowded Tel Aviv shopping mall.
1996 - British Prime Minister John Major said all of Hong Kong's permanent residents would be allowed visa-free entry into Britain after China took over in 1997.
